summary: Adding the LIAR-PLUS evidence/justification passage to the input (statement + speaker metadata + Evidence:<passage>) gives a marginal improvement over the metadata-only model on the held-out LIAR TEST set: macro-F1 0.655 -> 0.662 (+0.007), accuracy 0.655 -> 0.662 (+0.007), with AUC essentially flat (0.733 -> 0.721). This is NOT the several-point gain LIAR-PLUS reports for BERT/RoBERTa-scale models; on this small DistilBERT the metadata-only baseline already sits at the published performance ceiling, leaving little headroom. No ISOT regression. No evidence of label leakage.
how_to_read: The headline 'after' number uses retrieved evidence at inference time (the PolitiFact justification passage). That is a DIFFERENT, easier task than the claim-only task a bare user-typed statement represents. Report the two separately. The claim-only capability of this same model is the 'metadata_only_ablation' row below (0.642).

published_context.liar_binary_typical_range: 60-69% accuracy for BERT/RoBERTa-scale models across multiple papers
published_context.documented_ceiling: ~62-66% accuracy even with RoBERTa/SVM/XGBoost (a documented performance ceiling)
published_context.liar_plus_finding: Alhindi et al. (2018): statement+justification scores several points above statement-only, mainly demonstrated on larger models / dedicated evidence encoders
published_context.our_position: 0.662 accuracy / 0.662 macro-F1 sits at the upper end of the published 60-69% range; the justification gain we observe is within noise on DistilBERT
published_context.leakage_check: Only 2.3% of justification passages contain an explicit verdict phrase (LIAR-PLUS strips the ruling sentence). Our result stays inside the published range, i.e. nowhere near the 85% that would signal leakage.

before_metadata_only.description: Deployed stage-2 model (speaker metadata, no evidence), from backend/liar_test_metrics.json

after_with_justification.description: New stage-2 model trained AND evaluated with the LIAR-PLUS evidence clause

after_metadata_only_ablation.description: The SAME justification-trained model, evaluated on claim+metadata WITHOUT evidence (what a bare user-typed claim gets). Isolates how much the model relies on the evidence at inference.

with_justification_vs_before_metadata_mo.note: Marginal / within noise. Justification did not clear the published ceiling.

within_model_evidence_effect.note: Same weights, evidence input (0.6618) vs no-evidence input (0.6415). The evidence IS informative, but the justification-trained model is a little weaker at the bare-claim task, so the net gain over the metadata-only model is small.

isot_regression_check.note: Negligible catastrophic forgetting; ISOT in-domain performance preserved.

training_config.dataset: LIAR train + LIAR-PLUS justification (test.tsv fingerprints excluded from train)
training_config.epochs: converged at epoch 3 (valid macro-F1 peak 0.6689); epoch 4 overfits (0.6506)

best_configuration_reason: Highest macro-F1 (0.6618) and accuracy (0.6618) on LIAR test, the project's primary metric. AUC is marginally lower than the metadata-only model (0.7214 vs 0.7329).
reproduce: notebooks/03_train_liar_stage2.py (USE_JUSTIFICATION=True) then notebooks/04_build_eval_data.py (USE_JUSTIFICATION=True) then backend/evaluation.py. Requires LIAR-PLUS train2/val2/test2.tsv in LIAR_Dataset/ (raw.githubusercontent.com/Tariq60/LIAR-PLUS/master/dataset/tsv/).
